bottom_line: In DECISION, low-dose digoxin versus placebo did not significantly reduce the primary composite of total worsening heart failure events and cardiovascular death (rate ratio 0.81; 95% CI 0.61–1.07, P = 0.133).
implications: With 238 versus 291 primary-outcome events (rate ratio 0.81; 95% CI 0.61–1.07; P = 0.133), this trial does not support a statistically significant reduction in the composite endpoint with low-dose digoxin versus placebo over the reported follow-up. The confidence interval includes no effect and a potential reduction. Safety signals reported as serious adverse events were similar overall (19.9 vs 18.3 events per 100 patient-years; rate ratio 1.09; 95% CI 0.86–1.37).

major_points.text: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in the Netherlands.
major_points.quote: DECISION was an investigator-initiated, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, conducted at 43 sites in the Netherlands

major_points.text: Population: symptomatic chronic HF with LVEF ≤50%, including sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation, with target serum digoxin concentration 0.5–0.9 ng ml−1.
major_points.quote: 1,001 patients with symptomatic chronic heart failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 50% or less were randomized to low-dose digoxin or placebo, with a target serum digoxin concentration of 0.5–0.9 ng ml−1.

major_points.text: Primary outcome definition: total worsening HF events (hospitalizations or urgent visits) plus cardiovascular mortality.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a composite of total worsening heart failure events, defined as total hospitalizations or total urgent hospital visits for worsening heart failure and cardiovascular mortality.

major_points.text: Primary outcome result was not statistically significant.
major_points.quote: 238 primary-outcome events occurred in 131 of 500 patients in the digoxin group, and 291 primary-outcome events in 152 of 501 patients occurred in the placebo group (rate ratio 0.81; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.61–1.07, P = 0.133).

major_points.text: Safety/tolerability: serious adverse events overall were similar between groups.
major_points.quote: The number of serious adverse events (excluding primary and secondary endpoints) was similar between groups, that is 19.9 events per 100 patient-years in the digoxin group versus 18.3 events per 100 patient-years in the placebo group (rate ratio 1.09, 95% CI 0.86–1.37).

major_points.text: Subgroup finding: no difference by sex for effect on the primary endpoint.
major_points.quote: there were no differences with regard to the effect of digoxin on the primary endpoint between women and men (rate ratio digoxin versus placebo: 0.71 and 0.85, respectively, P value for interaction 0.61)

absolute_effects.text: Primary outcome: 238 events (15.7 per 100 patient-years) vs 291 events (19.3 per 100 patient-years).
absolute_effects.quote: Total worsening heart failure events and death from               238                    15.7                   291                     19.3

absolute_effects.text: Total worsening heart failure events: 155 (10.2 per 100 patient-years) vs 203 (13.5 per 100 patient-years).
Cardiovascular death: 83 (17) (5.5 per 100 patient-years) vs 88 (18) (5.8 per 100 patient-years).
All-cause death: 118 (24) (7.7 per 100 patient-years) vs 126 (25) (8.4 per 100 patient-years).

subgroups.text: Primary outcome assessed in 11 prespecified subgroups.
subgroups.quote: The primary outcome was assessed in 11 prespecified subgroups.

subgroups.text: Sex subgroup: women RR 0.71 (0.38–1.32) and men RR 0.85 (0.63–1.14), P interaction 0.610.
Heart rhythm subgroup: AF/AFl RR 0.76 (0.46–1.25) and SR RR 0.82 (0.59–1.14), P interaction 0.801.
Heart failure type subgroup: HFrEF (≤40%) RR 0.82 (0.60–1.13) and HFmrEF (EF >40%) RR 0.72 (0.42–1.24), P interaction 0.745.

harms.text: Serious adverse events overall were similar between groups.
Treatment-related serious adverse events were reported in 40 vs 25 patients (not significantly different).

harms.text: Study drug discontinuation for reasons other than death occurred in 92/382 vs 77/375 at end of study visit.

group and 77 of 375 patients (21%) in the placebo group had discon-
